Über HappyOps

HappyOps entwickelt moderne Softwarelösungen für mittelständische Industrieunternehmen in Europa. Unsere Kunden kommen aus unterschiedlichen Branchen, darunter der Glas, Metall, Kunststoff und Maschinenbauindustrie. Gemeinsam mit ihnen digitalisieren wir Produktionsprozesse und entwickeln individuelle Softwarelösungen, die täglich in realen Fabriken eingesetzt werden.

Wir sind ein profitables, eigenfinanziertes Softwareunternehmen mit einem vollständig remote arbeitenden Engineering Team. Unsere Kultur ist geprägt von Eigenverantwortung, direkter Kommunikation und kurzen Entscheidungswegen.

Über die Rolle

Wir suchen einen erfahrenen Senior Full Stack Softwareentwickler*in (f/m/d) mit verhandlungssicheren Deutsch- und Englischkenntnissen sowie sehr guten Kenntnissen (mindestens C1) in mindestens einer weiteren Sprache: Französisch, Spanisch oder Italienisch.

In dieser Rolle entwickelst du nicht nur Software, sondern arbeitest eng mit unseren internationalen Kunden zusammen, verstehst ihre Prozesse und setzt gemeinsam mit unserem Team moderne Lösungen für die produzierende Industrie um. Du begleitest Projekte von der ersten Anforderung bis zum produktiven Einsatz und verbindest technische Exzellenz mit pragmatischer Problemlösung.

Aufgaben

  • Entwicklung, Weiterentwicklung und Betrieb individueller Softwarelösungen für Kunden aus der produzierenden Industrie. Du verantwortest, was du entwickelst. You build it, you run it.

  • Umsetzung komplexer Businesslogik mit modernen Technologien und Softwarearchitekturen sowie kontinuierliche Optimierung bestehender Anwendungen.

  • Entwicklung intuitiver Web UIs, die komplexe Fertigungsprozesse einfach und effizient abbilden.

  • Entwicklung, Betrieb und Wartung skalierbarer Cloud und On Premise Anwendungen inklusive Monitoring, Logging und Fehleranalyse.

  • Entwicklung und Integration von Schnittstellen zu ERP Systemen, Manufacturing Software, Maschinensteuerungen, Sensoren und weiterer OT Infrastruktur.

  • Analyse technischer Anforderungen gemeinsam mit Projektmanagern und Kunden sowie Übersetzung dieser Anforderungen in robuste Softwarelösungen.

  • Enge Zusammenarbeit mit Kunden während des gesamten Projektverlaufs, von der Anforderungsaufnahme über die Implementierung bis zum produktiven Einsatz.

  • Kontinuierliche Verbesserung unserer Plattform, Entwicklungsprozesse und technischen Standards sowie aktive Mitgestaltung unserer Produkt und Technologie Roadmap.

Qualifikation

  • Mindestens 5 Jahre Berufserfahrung als Full Stack Softwareentwickler*in in einem professionellen Entwicklungsumfeld.

  • Sehr gute Kenntnisse in TypeScript, React, Node.js, Express.js, modernen Webtechnologien sowie im Schreiben automatisierter Tests.

  • Verhandlungssichere Deutsch- und Englischkenntnisse sowie mindestens C1-Kenntnisse in einer weiteren Sprache (Französisch, Spanisch oder Italienisch). Du kannst technische Anforderungen eigenständig mit internationalen Kunden besprechen und Workshops in diesen Sprachen durchführen.

  • Erfahrung mit Cloud Architekturen, APIs und modernen Softwareentwicklungsprozessen. Kenntnisse im Bereich Industrial IoT, Maschinenkommunikation oder Industrieprotokolle sind ein Plus.

  • Du arbeitest eigenverantwortlich, übernimmst Verantwortung für deine Lösungen und bringst Projekte zuverlässig zum Abschluss.

  • Du denkst pragmatisch, lernst schnell und hast Freude daran, komplexe technische Herausforderungen gemeinsam mit Kunden und dem Team zu lösen.

  • Du kannst technische Entscheidungen fundiert begründen, bringst eigene Ideen ein und bist gleichzeitig offen für neue Perspektiven und konstruktives Feedback.

  • Du arbeitest strukturiert, hast einen hohen Qualitätsanspruch und behältst auch in dynamischen Projekten den Überblick.

  • Du hast Freude an der engen Zusammenarbeit mit Kunden sowie mit unserem Gründungsteam und möchtest die technische Zukunft von HappyOps aktiv mitgestalten.

Benefits

  • Entwickle Software mit echtem Einfluss. Deine Lösungen werden täglich in Fabriken eingesetzt und helfen Unternehmen, produktiver, ressourcenschonender und wettbewerbsfähiger zu werden.

  • Arbeite an anspruchsvollen technischen Herausforderungen an der Schnittstelle zwischen Software, Maschinen, Daten und industriellen Prozessen.

  • Gestalte die technische und organisatorische Weiterentwicklung von HappyOps aktiv mit und bringe deine Ideen direkt ein.

  • Arbeite in einem kleinen, erfahrenen Engineering Team mit kurzen Entscheidungswegen, hoher Eigenverantwortung und direktem Austausch mit den Gründern.

  • Flexible Arbeitszeiten, vollständig remote und eine Kultur, die Ergebnisse höher bewertet als Anwesenheit.

  • Freie Wahl deiner Entwicklungsumgebung und deines IT Equipments, damit du mit den Werkzeugen arbeiten kannst, die für dich am besten funktionieren.

  • Ein attraktives Gehalt sowie die Möglichkeit, dich fachlich und persönlich in einem wachsenden Softwareunternehmen weiterzuentwickeln.

Die Gehaltsspanne für diese Position liegt, abhängig von Erfahrung und Qualifikation, zwischen 70.000 € und 100.000 € brutto pro Jahr.

Bei HappyOps zählen für uns Kompetenz, Motivation und Teamfit. Wir begrüßen Bewerbungen unabhängig von Alter, Geschlecht, sexueller Identität, ethnischer Herkunft, Religion oder einer Behinderung.

Klingt die Rolle spannend? Dann freuen wir uns auf deine Bewerbung. Auch wenn du nicht jede einzelne Anforderung erfüllst, möchten wir dich ausdrücklich ermutigen, dich zu bewerben. Sende uns einfach deinen Lebenslauf sowie deinen frühestmöglichen Eintrittstermin und deine Gehaltsvorstellung.

Kennst du jemanden, der perfekt zu uns passen könnte? Für jede erfolgreiche Empfehlung, die zu einer Einstellung führt, zahlen wir eine Empfehlungsprämie von 1.500 €.

Hi I’m Abhik, Ashby's Co-Founder and VP of Engineering. This role is close to my heart because, as someone who can both design and code, it’s where I’ve always done my best work, but also where I was seen as a rebel and an outsider. I want folks like me to feel at home at Ashby, and so I made Design Engineering a formal role and department that works closely with me. Our first hire was over five years ago, and we’re doubling the team from five to over ten in the next year.

This role truly expects you to design and code. Design Engineer at Ashby isn’t just a Frontend Engineer with new branding, nor is it a Designer vibe coding prototypes. Combining excellence in both is where magic happens. I found that when I put my best effort into both the design and technical implementation of a feature, I had a nimbleness and creativity that was hard to achieve when I did only one or the other. For instance, the UX and UI I envisioned often influenced the data model's design and flexibility, while the understanding of technology's capabilities often simplified or improved the design. This role embraces that.

You’ll work on our most challenging design problems, help others improve their designs by expanding and enhancing our in-house design system, and consult on bespoke design work needed by Product Engineers. To ground it with examples, Design Engineers at Ashby have:

  • Redesigned our mobile web app by talking with customers who use it often, wireframing new flows, implementing its design system, and using that system to turn the wireframes into a polished UI.

  • Built a set of flexible, composable components in our design system that allow other engineers to build beautiful, consistent setup wizards across our product easily.

  • Helped a Product Engineer improve the information hierarchy and scannability of their design for viewing a candidate’s assessments. Recruiters can quickly parse information and pick out anomalies.

The Design Engineer role is more common today than five years ago, but I believe Ashby offers a unique opportunity that few can match:

  • You work on a product at scale, not at an early-stage startup struggling to find users and get feedback on what you’ve designed and built. At Ashby, your work will touch over 100,000 weekly active users, millions of candidates per week, and notable customers like Notion, Linear, Shopify, and Snowflake. You’ll get to test out ideas with our own recruiting team and hiring managers who use Ashby every day (like me), and often hear customer feedback as early as the day you release.

  • This role has always had the commitment of both Benji (CEO & Co-Founder) and me: I’ve held the role, steadfastly championed it since we started hiring in 2020, and haven’t diluted its responsibilities as we’ve grown (in fact, we’ve doubled down).

  • You get to shape the UI and UX of a powerful and complex product. Our users need software that helps them move quickly while adapting to their unique workflows and preferences. As a result, our UI isn’t a simple chatbox, but it can’t rely on a sea of knobs and dials either. It needs to feel approachable to someone using it for the first time while offering increasingly powerful ways to customize and automate their work.

Why You Shouldn’t Apply

Design Engineers come in many flavors, not all of which fit our model. Here are some reasons you might not enjoy the role:

  • You only want to work on design systems. While improving our design system is one of many responsibilities, you won’t be able to work on it exclusively.

  • You like to do extensive research and user testing before implementation. The beauty of being part-Engineer is that you can build conviction by shipping to a subset of users (including our own team) and gathering feedback!

  • You want everything to be perfect before it gets into a user’s hands. One of the drivers of our success is that we ship fast. While we appreciate the strive for perfection, we also realize it doesn’t need to be achieved all at once; instead, we iterate over time, often letting user feedback and business needs drive prioritization.

  • You don’t have excellent taste and execution in visual design. Design Engineers set the bar for visual design in our app and continually improve it, pushing its boundaries with each new feature or redesign.

  • You need company-driven process and structure to get your projects across the finish line. Sprint planning and well-defined project management processes are things you need or look to others to lead. You’d rather focus on the design and technical details.

  • You only want to do exciting work. We’re building a team of kind, collaborative folks. Customer issues and investigations are distributed across the team, including our high-level ICs.

What Seniority/Level To Apply For

We’ve posted levels from Junior to Staff. The higher the level, the more experience and alignment with the role we expect when reviewing your application and while interviewing. Please apply to the one that sets the right expectations.

  • Junior Design Engineer - You should have no more than 2 years of industry experience as a designer or engineer. We want to see projects (personal or professional) with at least a couple of users that showcase great visual taste and burgeoning talent in both UI/UX and Engineering.

  • Design Engineer - This posting covers both Mid and Senior levels. You have 2+ years of continuous experience (e.g., internships don’t count) as an Engineer or a Designer. You have good proficiency in both Design and Engineering, with exceptional proficiency in the discipline you practice full-time. Regardless of which discipline you’re coming from, we expect experience designing products and shipping code to hundreds of users (even if through side projects).

  • Staff Design Engineer (This Posting) - We’re looking for folks who’ve practiced our flavor of Design Engineering professionally. It may not be through a formal title, but you’ve made major contributions to a design system and designed and implemented features for hundreds of users and iterated on them through user feedback.

Internally, we do not use these titles, but Engineers are leveled based on proficiency (which you can read about here).

What We’re Building

As engineers, we are used to tooling that makes us better at what we do. When we started Ashby, we saw the opposite with Talent Acquisition software. Recruiting teams were leveling up how they did their work, but instead of software meeting this new standard, it held them back.

Scheduling a final round is an excellent example. Recruiting teams wanted to schedule candidates faster, track interviewer preparation and quality, and do it with half the headcount. A recruiter needed to manually collect availability from the candidate, identify qualified interviewers, perform “Calendar Tetris” to find who is available to interview the candidate, schedule on the earliest date possible, and make any last-minute adjustments as availability changed. They must do this while considering the interview load on each individual and whether interviewers need to be trained and shadowing others. TA software didn’t help.

As hiring managers, we know TA is a critical function, and as engineers, we know software can do better. So, we built and continue to build Ashby to give TA teams the highest standard of tooling. Software that’s intelligent and powerful. Software that provides insights into where they’re failing and automates or simplifies many of the tasks they’re underwater with. We want other functions and departments to be jealous of what TA teams can do with Ashby, and today they often are!

As we’ve set the standard for excellence in TA software, HR teams have pulled us into solving their problems in areas like onboarding and performance management.

Engineering Culture

Our engineering culture is motivated by Benji’s (my Co-founder and CEO) and my belief that a small, talented team, given the right environment, can build high-quality software fast (and work regular hours!). We do it through:

  • Minimal process with ownership over decisions normally made by product and design

  • Natural collaboration and deliberate communication

  • Investing in tools and abstractions that give us leverage

  • Putting effort into building a diverse team

Minimal Process & Lots of Ownership

The best engineers we’ve worked with delivered reliably magical outcomes. They took customer problems and relentlessly drove them to solutions that were not only successful but often brilliant and creative. While they did this with minimal oversight, stakeholders were never in the dark as to what was going on, and no setback was a surprise.

Traditional product-development processes aren’t meant for the best engineers. Their purpose is to create consistent outcomes regardless of the engineer’s skill. But, consistency comes at the expense of an engineer’s time and freedom—both ingredients necessary to generate those magical outcomes. As a result, process stifles the best engineers and doesn’t give others the opportunity to practice the behaviors that made the best engineers the “best.”

At Ashby, we want to build an environment that encourages every engineer to be their best. So, at Ashby, every Engineer runs their project. Product Managers (and Designers) build strategy, do customer research, and hand off problem briefs to Engineers. Engineers take on the rest: they research the problem, write product specs, build wireframes, and implement their solution end-to-end. We rely on engineers, not process, to push information outward to the relevant folks (e.g., Product Managers) and pull folks in to help (e.g., Designers, Infra). It’s a new level of ownership for many engineers, but we’d rather an engineer fail a bit and coach up their skills than use process as a crutch. Not everyone succeeds in our culture, but those who do thrive.

Collaboration is Natural & Communication is Deliberate

Our engineering team consists of lifelong learners who are talented but also humble and kind (meet them here!). These attributes create an environment where collaboration happens naturally. We combine this with research, prototyping, and written proposals to see around corners and get feedback from the team across time zones. Focus time is something that we hold sacred, and, with thoughtful and deliberate communication, engineers are in <2h meetings per week (I wrote about it here).

Today, 25% of engineers and 50% of our engineering leaders at Ashby are from underrepresented groups. We are taking conscious steps to improve, like sourcing diverse candidates, providing generous paid family leave, no leetcode interviews, and more.

We also meet in person at least twice a year, once as a department and once as a company. You also have a small budget to meet up with folks in your city/region.

Increase Leverage, not Team Size

We built Ashby with the quality, breadth, and depth that many customers would expect from much larger teams over larger time scales. We’ve done this through investment in:

  • Great developer tooling. Our CI/CD takes ~10m, and we deploy at least 15x a day. A debugger that works out of the box. Everyone on the team has contributed to our developer experience .

  • Building blocks to create powerful and customizable products fast. At the core of Ashby is a set of common components (analytics modeling and query language, policy engine, workflow engine, design system) that we constantly improve. Each improvement to a common component cascades throughout our app (short video below).

  • AI-powered tooling. We think of AI as a way to automate the mundane parts of building and maintaining high-quality software. We use a combination of third-party and internally built tools that, for instance, auto-triage customer issues, suggest fixes, prototype ideas, generate production-ready code, and conduct code reviews. Engineers have an unlimited token budget (but are not measured on it). We write in detail about our philosophy, current use of AI, and future plans for AI in Engineering here.

Here’s an impromptu quote from Arjun in our company Slack of what it’s like to build a feature at Ashby:

And a demo of one of these building blocks:

Put Effort into Diversity

Diverse teams drive innovation and better outcomes. Having seen my mother and partner build their careers as minority women in non-diverse fields, I want to make sure Ashby creates opportunities for the next generation of engineers from underrepresented groups.

Today, 25% of engineers and 50% of our engineering leaders at Ashby are from underrepresented groups. We are taking conscious steps to improve, like sourcing diverse candidates, providing generous paid family leave, no leetcode interviews, and more.

Work-Life Balance: It’s A Marathon, Not a Sprint

The intensity of work at Ashby should feel like a marathon, not a sprint (nor speed-walking). We work with urgency and ambition to build excellent software, but we don’t need to prove out a new software category or product-market fit. That requires ingenuity and thoughtfulness, and that doesn’t happen with unrealistic deadlines or sleepless nights.

Our remote, low-meeting, high-ownership culture gives you a lot of flexibility in how you structure your days and weeks. In practice, that means you keep your own hours, but there will be moments of intensity, like launching your feature at our annual user conference. We offer unlimited PTO, and you actually get to use it. Some of our most exceptional engineers take almost 30 days of vacation per year.

This way of working allows many of us on the team to be active parents, including Benji and me. I block off 1.5 hours every morning to spend with my daughter and drop her off at school. Mujda (Product Engineer) puts it best in an article about us: “I can say that Ashby is a great place to be a mom… No one bats an eye if I have to take my kid to a doctor’s appointment or have to work weird hours because childcare fell through.”

Interview Process

At Ashby, our team and interview process want to help you show your best self. We’ll dive into past projects and simulate working together through pair programming, designing, writing design system specs collaboratively, and discussing decisions. There are no leetcode or whiteboard exercises.

Our interview process is three rounds:

  • Introduction call with me (30m, live). Be prepared to screen-share examples of your work.

  • A second round where we either do a technical screen (1h, live) or a design take-home (~3h async, 30m live)

  • Three interviews, a deep dive into a past design system or design project, a design system interview, and the interview we didn’t do in the second round: technical screen or design take-home. (3h, live)

Depending on our leadership team’s bandwidth, we may start with an additional 30m screen with a recruiter.

I will be your main point of contact and prep you for interviews. Each round will have written guidance so you know what to expect. You’ll meet 3-4 people in Design Engineering (with 5-15 minutes in each interview to ask them questions). If we don’t give an offer, we’ll provide feedback!

Your First Three Months at Ashby

We want an exceptional onboarding experience for every new hire. At Ashby, your dev environment is set up with a single script, you push your first product change on day one, and you spend the rest of your time shipping product changes that give you a tour of our codebase and best practices. The product changes increase in scope and ambiguity from simple copy changes to the delivery of a prominent, impactful feature. Your manager will do a 30, 60, and 90-day review to give feedback and calibrate on how we work together.

It’s a team effort to get you successfully onboarded; you’ll have a peer paired with you to answer questions, pair program, and check in often to see if you need help. The rest of the team will run training sessions on our culture, product, engineering process, and technical architecture.

Technology Stack

Our tech stack is TypeScript (frontend & backend), React, GraphQL API, Node.js, Postgres, and Redis. Depending on the level you’re applying for and your past experience, we expect, at a minimum, good proficiency with TypeScript, React, and CSS. Proficiency with backend technologies is a plus, as it allows you to work without coordinating with Product Engineers.

Benefits

  • Competitive salary and equity.

  • 10-year exercise window for stock options. You shouldn’t feel pressure to purchase stock options if you leave Ashby —do it when you feel financially comfortable.

  • Unlimited PTO, and we will encourage you to take it.

  • A minimum of 12 weeks of fully paid parental leave, covered by Ashby. For folks outside the US, it may be longer to be in line with regional requirements.

  • Generous equipment, software, and office furniture budget. Get what you need to be happy and productive!

  • $100/month education budget with more expensive items (like conferences) covered with manager approval.

  • $250/month tool budget plus access to Claude, Cursor, and Codex with generous token budgets.

  • If you’re in the US, we offer top-tier health insurance for you and your dependents, with 100% of premiums covered by Ashby. In other countries, we provide high-quality supplemental health insurance for you and your dependents, also fully covered by us.

Ashby’s success hinges on hiring great people and creating an environment where we can be happy, feel challenged, and do our best work. We’re being deliberate about building that environment from the ground up. I hope that excites you enough to apply.

Waarom deze rol bestaat

De meeste AI-projecten halen productie nooit. Zes maanden verder, budget verdubbeld, scope gehalveerd, en wat er ligt is een presentatie in plaats van software die eindgebruikers omarmen.

Wij doen het anders. Een werkende POC in zeven dagen, op echte data van de klant. Daarna in weken naar productie. Die belofte houdt alleen stand als de mensen die hem waarmaken scherp zijn.

Met agentic coding tools zoals Claude Code en Codex komt er sneller iets werkends uit dan ooit. Daardoor verschuift het werk van bouwen naar regie voeren. De vraag achterhalen, de juiste oplossing ontwerpen, AI en engineering slim inzetten, en de kwaliteit bewaken. Daarom zoeken we iemand die tussen developer en consultant in zit. Technisch sterk genoeg om zelf te bouwen en te beoordelen of iets deugt, sterk genoeg aan de voorkant om de vraag achter de vraag te vinden, en verantwoordelijk tot het live staat en live blijft.

AI schrijft bij ons veel. Verantwoordelijkheid kun je niet uitbesteden. Alles wat jouw naam draagt, heb je zelf gelezen, gecontroleerd en begrepen voordat het de deur uitgaat.

Taken

Er zijn twee manieren waarop onze klanten bij ons bouwen, en jij doet ze allebei.

Wij bouwen

Een klant stapt binnen met een proof of concept. Zeven dagen, een scherp gekaderde scope.

Jij ownt die POC. Jij vraagt uit wat er echt nodig is, jij bepaalt wat er wel en niet in gaat, jij bouwt hem op hun echte data, en jij neemt de klant stap voor stap mee in de demo. Daarna bouw je het in weken uit tot MVP. Vanaf dat moment doe je het niet meer alleen. Je haalt je team erbij, neemt ze mee in wat het moet worden en bouwt samen verder. Vervolgens maak je het productieklaar, met auth, monitoring en CI/CD. Jij blijft er eigenaar van.

De klant bouwt, wij borgen

Bij een groeiend deel van onze klanten bouwt hun eigen team met Claude Code, Codex en Cursor. Wij reviewen elke pull request, tekenen elke release en zetten de productieomgeving op, volgens onze standaarden en zonder dat ze erop hoeven wachten.

Daar is je rol anders. Je zit bij hun product owners, delivery lead en developers aan tafel, je kijkt kritisch mee met wat ze maken, en jij borgt dat het veilig en productiewaardig live komt. Je bouwt minder zelf en je beoordeelt meer. Dat vraagt dat je kunt uitleggen waarom iets niet deugt zonder dat iemand zich aangevallen voelt, en dat je ze in gewone taal meeneemt in hoe het wel hoort.

Je hebt je eigen klantportfolio en bent hun aanspreekpunt binnen SevenLab. Je begeleidt discovery sessies en workshops om tot richting en prioriteiten te komen, en je schat in wat je zelf doet, wat je samen oppakt en wanneer een specialist moet aanhaken.

Vereisten

Must have

  • meerdere jaren ervaring met het bouwen van webapplicaties of softwareproducten;
  • je hebt zelf software naar productie gebracht die nu live draait en door klanten wordt gebruikt, en je kunt het laten zien;
  • je kunt in een week in je eentje iets werkends neerzetten op echte data, en je weet wat je bewust buiten scope houdt om dat te halen;
  • je hebt eerder in een rol gezeten waarin techniek en klantcontact samenkwamen, en je kunt een klantgesprek leiden en de vraag achter de vraag vinden;
  • je bent kritisch op codekwaliteit, structuur, testbaarheid en onderhoudbaarheid, ook bij code die een AI-tool oplevert. Niets gaat langs jou zonder dat je het hebt getest en beoordeeld;
  • je kunt iets veilig live zetten en live houden: deployment, monitoring, security, en weten wat je doet als het misgaat;
  • je denkt in systemen. Kom je iets voor de derde keer tegen, dan los je het niet voor de derde keer op. Dan bouw je iets zodat het niet meer gebeurt;
  • je zoekt het eerst zelf uit in de documentatie, de code en de logs. Blijft er een vraag over, dan stel je hem met een hypothese erbij zodat de ander in één keer kan antwoorden;
  • je zet vaagheid om in richting, structuur en resultaat;
  • je communiceert scherp: je legt technische keuzes uit aan mensen zonder technische achtergrond, en je geeft feedback op andermans werk zodat ze er wat mee kunnen;
  • professioneel Nederlands en Engels, gesproken en geschreven.

Nice to have

  • ervaring met release-governance als specialisme: approvals, signing, rollback;
  • ervaring in gereguleerde sectoren zoals zorg of de publieke sector;
  • open source bijdragen op je naam.

Voor wie dit is

  • je wil eigenaar zijn van het hele traject, van eerste gesprek tot wat er live staat, en je vindt het prettig dat het jouw naam is die eraan hangt;
  • snel en goed zijn bij jou geen tegenpolen. Je haalt dat door scope scherp te houden en te weten waar je niet op moet inkorten;
  • je wil voorop lopen, probeert nieuwe dingen uit en wil beter worden dan je gisteren was;
  • je denkt verder dan "kunnen we dit bouwen". Je vraagt je ook af wat het oplevert en wat de slimste route is;
  • als er iets stukgaat, ben jij degene die het meldt voordat iemand het vraagt.

Voor wie dit niet is

  • de developer die het liefst de hele dag in zijn editor zit en klantcontact vermijdt;
  • de consultant die adviseert wat een klant moet bouwen en daarna weg is. Wij zijn verantwoordelijk tot en met productie;
  • iemand die veel prototypes maakt die daarna blijven liggen;
  • iemand die de output van een chatbot doorstuurt zonder hem zelf te lezen. AI gebruiken doen we allemaal, de hele dag. Het ongelezen doorgeven van wat eruit komt is iets anders;
  • iemand die een vraag bij een ander neerlegt voordat hij de documentatie heeft opengeslagen of zelf heeft getest.

Waar je mee werkt

Fullstack JavaScript en TypeScript, Vue en Nuxt, PostgreSQL en Drizzle, Claude Code en vergelijkbare agentic tooling, CI/CD, monitoring. We draaien op NVIDIA-infrastructuur en op Scaleway voor Europese data-residency. We zijn ISO 27001-gecertificeerd en onze klanten zitten in sectoren waar dat niet vrijblijvend is.

Benefits

  • veel ruimte voor moderne AI-tooling en nieuwe manieren van software bouwen, en invloed op hoe we oplossingen ontwerpen en opleveren;
  • een team van sterke specialisten waarmee je kunt sparren en waar je op kunt leunen wanneer iets dieper of complexer wordt;
  • bruto maandsalaris tussen €4.300 en €5.600 op basis van 40 uur;
  • 28 vakantiedagen, 10% pensioenregeling en onze Super SevenLab dagen.
  • een omgeving waarin snelheid, kwaliteit en innovatie samenkomen.

Ons proces

Na je sollicitatie plannen we eerst een korte remote kennismaking. Daarna volgt een gesprek op kantoor met een praktische case of assessment.

In die case bepaal jij wat je zou uitvragen, wat je in en buiten scope zet om het af te krijgen, wat er niet deugt aan wat er ligt, en wat er moet gebeuren voordat dit veilig live kan. Je mag AI gebruiken zoveel je wil. We kijken ook naar de vragen die je ons stelt.

Neem voorbeelden mee van iets dat je zelf live hebt gebracht en dat klanten gebruiken.

Hoe je solliciteert

Stuur ons je CV, samen met een antwoord op deze vraag. Een paar alinea's is genoeg:

Beschrijf iets dat je hebt gebouwd met AI en live hebt gezet, en dat daarna een serieus probleem bleek te hebben. Hoe kwam je erachter, wat deed je eraan, en hoe zorgde je dat het niet nog een keer kon gebeuren?

Descriptif du poste

Nous cherchons quelqu’un qui ne code plus « à la main » par défaut. Le poste consiste à construire, seul ou en binôme, des applications web complètes (front, back, data, déploiement) en s’appuyant massivement sur les outils d’IA générative — et à faire évoluer nos pratiques de delivery en conséquence.

Ce n’est pas un poste de développeur qui « utilise un peu Copilot ». C’est un poste de builder qui pilote des agents de code, spécifie clairement, itère vite, et garde la responsabilité de la qualité, de la sécurité et de la maintenabilité de ce qui est livré.

Missions

Construire

  • Concevoir et livrer des applications produites de bout en bout : interface, API, base de données, intégrations, déploiement.
  • Passer d’un besoin métier à un prototype fonctionnel en jours, pas en semaines ; puis industrialiser ce qui doit l’être.
  • Intégrer des briques IA (LLM, agents, RAG) dans les applications quand c’est pertinent.

Piloter l’IA

  • Utiliser au quotidien des outils de développement assisté et agentique (type Claude Code, Cursor, Copilot, agents autonomes) sur l’intégralité du cycle : spécification, génération, tests, revue, documentation, refactoring.
  • Écrire et maintenir les prompts, instructions de projet, règles et contextes qui rendent ces outils fiables et reproductibles sur nos bases de code.
  • Rester en veille active sur les modèles, outils et protocoles (MCP, agents, évaluation) et les tester rapidement.

Faire évoluer les méthodes

  • Adapter nos pratiques agiles à un contexte où le coût de production du code s’effondre : cycles très courts, spécification comme livrable principal, revue humaine centrée sur l’architecture et la sécurité plutôt que sur la syntaxe.
  • Documenter et partager ces pratiques avec les équipes produit et R&D ; former ponctuellement des collègues.

Sécuriser

  • Appliquer les bonnes pratiques de développement sécurisé (OWASP, gestion des secrets, dépendances, revue du code généré) dans un contexte d’éditeur certifié ISO 27001.
  • Comprendre les enjeux spécifiques du code produit par IA : hallucinations de librairies, dettes cachées, données sensibles dans les prompts.

Profil recherché

Indispensable

  • 3 à 6 ans d’expérience en développement web full stack (JavaScript/TypeScript, Python ou équivalent ; une stack moderne type React/Next, Node ou FastAPI, PostgreSQL, conteneurs).
  • Pratique intensive et démontrable des outils d’IA pour coder : capacité à montrer des projets réels construits de cette manière, à expliquer ce qui a marché et ce qui a cassé.
  • Autonomie forte : capable de prendre un besoin flou et de livrer quelque chose d’utilisable sans supervision rapprochée.
  • Rigueur sur les fondamentaux : Git, tests, CI/CD, revue de code, sécurité de base.
  • Bonne compréhension des méthodes agiles (Scrum, Kanban) et regard critique sur leur adaptation au développement assisté par IA.

Apprécié

  • Expérience ou forte appétence pour la cybersécurité : environnement SOC, produit de détection, secure SDLC, pentest, ou simple culture personnelle solide du domaine.
  • Contributions open source, side projects, portfolio public d’applications « vibecodées ».
  • Expérience d’intégration de LLM dans des produits (API, agents, évaluation).
  • Anglais professionnel.

État d’esprit

  • Curiosité et vitesse d’apprentissage supérieures à la moyenne.
  • Confort avec l’incertitude et les outils encore instables.
  • Sens du produit : comprend pourquoi on construit, pas seulement comment.
  • Honnêteté intellectuelle sur les limites de l’IA et de son propre code.

Déroulement des entretiens

1er entretien RH en visio

2ème entretien avec les équipes techniques en visio

3ème entretien avec la direction sur site

Qui sont-ils ?

Gatewatcher fait entrer les opérations de cybersécurité dans l’ère de la décision. Fort de son expertise reconnue en NDR, l’éditeur français associe détection avancée et IA agentique au sein de Decision Center, une plateforme capable de corréler les signaux provenant de l’ensemble du SOC pour les transformer en décisions explicables et actionnables. Du réseau au SIEM, de l’EDR au Cloud et à l’identité, Gatewatcher aide les organisations à passer plus rapidement de la détection à l’action, tout en garantissant maîtrise, traçabilité et autonomie

About the Role

We're looking for a Senior Product Security Engineer to lead the design and implementation of secure, scalable, and trustworthy products across AlphaSense's AI-native platform. You'll work closely with architects, engineering, and product teams to embed security by design throughout the software development lifecycle.

This role sits at the intersection of AI/ML security, secure architecture, threat modeling, and customer-facing assurance — defining the standards, automation, and frameworks that enable secure, intelligent products at scale.

What You’ll Do:

AI Security & Enablement (30%)

  • Architect and enforce security controls for AI/ML systems — model training, data pipelines, inference environments, and agentic workflows.
  • Identify and mitigate AI-specific attack vectors: prompt injection, data poisoning, model inversion, model theft.
  • Implement model provenance, integrity, and auditability controls for responsible, secure AI operations.
  • Align AI security with governance and compliance teams against frameworks like NIST AI RMF and the EU AI Act.

Secure Architecture & Development Lifecycle (30%)

  • Embed security throughout the software and AI development lifecycle, partnering with architects, engineering, and product across AlphaSense's application and cloud ecosystems.
  • Ensure security, privacy, and compliance by design.
  • Define and maintain secure development standards, guidance, and best practices.

Threat Modeling & Security Review (20%)

  • Lead threat modeling, secure design reviews, and risk assessments across the software development lifecycle.
  • Build and maintain security automation and governance that integrates into development workflows.

Customer-Facing Security Assurance (10%)

  • Produce customer-facing security assurance — security questionnaire responses, security whitepapers, and trust collateral — that unblocks enterprise deals.
  • Represent product security in customer, cross-functional, and leadership discussions.

Leadership (10%)

  • Mentor teams on secure coding, AI risk management, and secure design.
  • Promote a security-first culture through advocacy, documentation, and training.

  • Deep understanding of secure SDLC, threat modeling, and secure architecture design.
  • Ability to read and review code to inform threat models and design reviews.
  • Experience securing AI/ML pipelines, data workflows, and model-serving infrastructure, with working knowledge of AI/LLM security (prompt injection, model integrity, provenance).
  • Proven expertise with cloud security concepts and best practices across multi-cloud environments.
  • Familiarity with DevSecOps and CI/CD environments.
  • Familiarity with encryption fundamentals — symmetric and asymmetric cryptography, TLS/mTLS, key management, and secrets handling.
  • Understanding of authentication and authorization patterns in modern applications: OAuth 2.0, OIDC, SAML, RBAC, and ABAC.
  • Demonstrated ability to drive cross-functional security initiatives — partnering with engineering, product, and compliance to embed security into roadmaps, influence architectural decisions, and align stakeholders across boundaries.

Nice to Have

  • Proficiency in Python, Java, and/or JavaScript for security automation and tooling.
  • Container and orchestration security (Kubernetes runtime protection).
  • Software supply chain security and artifact integrity verification.
  • Experience with bug bounty programs — triaging findings, driving root-cause analysis, and turning results into systemic security improvements.
  • Familiarity with compliance and governance frameworks (SOC 2, ISO 27001, NIST 800-53, NIST AI RMF).

Vous analysez les pratiques réelles, observez plusieurs cas concrets de delivery et croisez les points de vue des parties prenantes afin d'établir un diagnostic objectivé et de formuler des recommandations opérationnelles et priorisées.

Vos principales responsabilités1. Analyser l'existant

  • Prendre connaissance des audits et analyses déjà réalisés, notamment sur les Design Tokens.

  • Consolider les enseignements disponibles et identifier les hypothèses à approfondir côté Produit et Tech.

  • Éviter les investigations redondantes et concentrer l'analyse sur l'intégration du Design System dans le delivery.

2. Auditer la chaîne Design → Code → Produit

  • Analyser le parcours d'un besoin Produit, de la conception à la mise en production et à la maintenance.

  • Suivre plusieurs cas réels de bout en bout pour identifier les étapes fluides, les ruptures, les temps d'attente et les contournements.

  • Évaluer l'articulation entre les ressources Design, les bibliothèques techniques et les produits en production.

  • Examiner les pratiques de consommation, de contribution, de réutilisation et de création de composants locaux.

3. Évaluer l'adoption et la couverture technique

  • Analyser l'utilisation effective du Design System par les équipes et les produits.

  • Comparer les niveaux de couverture et les pratiques entre plusieurs offres numériques.

  • Étudier les spécificités des environnements Web, iOS et Android.

  • Identifier les écarts entre les composants conçus, leur implémentation technique et leur utilisation en production.

  • Exploiter les données disponibles pour établir une première mesure de référence de l'adoption.

4. Analyser le fonctionnement Produit, Tech et delivery

  • Comprendre les modalités de développement et de maintenance des composants.

  • Évaluer les capacités mobilisées, leur disponibilité et leur pérennité.

  • Analyser les arbitrages entre les besoins transverses du Design System et les priorités des roadmaps Produit.

  • Identifier les difficultés liées aux responsabilités, à la contribution, à la coordination et à la continuité technique.

  • Distinguer les besoins de mutualisation des besoins propres aux produits et aux plateformes.

About the Role

We are hiring our first Director of Go-to-Market Engineering.

Perk's revenue organisation is 800 people selling to more than 10,000 companies. Behind them sits a CRM, an enrichment and signal stack, a growing set of AI agents - and a lot of manual work that no longer needs to exist. Your job is to remove it and to build the automated systems that replace it.

You will own GTM Engineering end-to-end: which tools we use, how the architecture fits together, what gets built, and what it does for revenue. You report to the VP of Revenue Operations, lead a small senior team across Europe and North America, and work across SDR, Account Executive, and Account Management - a few high-impact projects each quarter.

This is a player-coach role, and we mean it. You will be in Clay, in the orchestration logic, in the agent workflows, building alongside a team doing the same. You're using your experience to guide and coach them to accelerate the pace.

The other half of the job is commercial. The best GTM engineers we have met can sit with a regional Sales VP, work out why their pipeline isn't converting, and leave with the right thing to build. That instinct matters more to us than any single tool on a CV.

What You'll Do

Own the strategy and the stack

  • Define Perk's GTM engineering architecture - how CRM, enrichment, signal, sequencing, orchestration and data layers fit together.

  • Make the tooling calls: what we adopt, what we consolidate, what we retire, and why it pays for itself.

  • Set the roadmap with the VP of Revenue Operations, Sales leadership, and the Revenue Systems and Data teams.

  • Establish the standards the team builds to - version control, documentation, testing, and rollback.

Build, hands-on

  • Design and build in Clay: tables, waterfall enrichment, AI columns, webhooks and API integrations in production.

  • Own the orchestration layer - the logic deciding which records enter a workflow, when, and on what criteria. This is where GTM automation succeeds or fails.

  • Build agentic workflows on modern LLM and agent tooling to take research, qualification, summarisation and data entry off people entirely.

  • Write the code the job needs - Python, SQL, SOQL or TypeScript.

Automate across SDR, AE, and AM

  • Own account prospecting automation globally: TAM sourcing, enrichment, ICP and intent scoring, prioritisation and distribution.

  • Give AEs their selling time back - CRM autofill, quoting, meeting prep, opportunity hygiene, first outbounds.

  • Build account intelligence for Account Management: risk signals, whitespace, account planning.

  • Take each project from prototype to production properly - instrumented and validated before it scales.

Bridge commercial and technical

  • Turn commercial problems into technical architecture, and technical output into impact a revenue VPs recognises.

  • Understand Perk's revenue goals and how to leverage AI capabilities for us to achieve them quicker and more efficiently.

  • Understand and drive clear and tangible commercial outcomes. For example, how to reduce the time that quota-carrying roles spend on non-core activities such as account research, be able to quantify the impact, and clearly communicate the outcomes to leadership.

Build the team

  • Lead and grow a small, senior team across Europe and North America.

  • Set clear ownership, and the review discipline that makes shipping fast also means shipping safely.

  • Grow the team's technical depth and commercial judgement in equal measure.

What Will Make You Successful

Experience

  • Deep background across Revenue Operations, GTM Engineering, Sales Systems, Growth Engineering, or an adjacent technical commercial function in B2B SaaS

  • Proven track record in GTM Engineering specifically, with delivery at real scale — systems hundreds of sellers relied on, not a pilot for one team

  • Time as both a builder and a leader. This role needs both.

Technical craft

  • Clay expertise in production - complex tables, waterfall enrichment, webhook integrations and AI column logic that revenue teams actually depended on.

  • Deep Salesforce fluency: the data model, integration patterns, and where the constraints really are.

  • Working proficiency in code — Python, SQL, SOQL, TypeScript or equivalent. You pull your own data. Not all coding languages are necessary, but proficiency in one or some is required.

  • Architecture instincts: you build for scale, monitoring and recovery, not just for the first successful run.

  • Depth across several layers of the modern GTM stack - enrichment and data (Apollo, Clearbit, ZoomInfo, Cognism, PredictLeads), signal and intent (6sense, Bombora, UserGems), sequencing (Outreach, Salesloft), orchestration (n8n, Make, Workato), data infrastructure (Snowflake, dbt, BigQuery) and LLM and agent tooling. Nobody has all of it. We care that you have real depth somewhere and can learn the rest quickly.

Commercial instinct

  • You judge your work by whether it moved a commercial metric, not by whether it shipped.

  • You have the credibility with Sales leaders to scope the right build - and to say when automation is the wrong answer.

  • You understand the funnel end to end: TAM, ICP, pipeline generation, conversion, expansion, and the economics underneath.

Nice to have

  • Having stood up a GTM engineering function at a high-growth SaaS business, ideally above $100M ARR.

  • Experience taking an automation programme from pilot to global production, including what you learned when it got bumpy.

  • Multi-region GTM experience across EMEA and North America.

Why This Role

GTM Engineering is a discipline being written right now, and most companies are still treating it as a tooling function. This is the chance to own it properly, the stack, the architecture, the build, and the commercial outcome across a $300M+ revenue business with 800 people in the field, a genuine appetite for automation, and the budget and executive backing to move fast.

You would be the first person in this seat, with real systems and real data to work with rather than a blank page, and the freedom to decide what Perk's automation layer should look like. There is a lot to go after, the problems are interesting, and the impact is immediate and visible.

If you want to build the automation layer of a commercial engine at this scale and you want to still have your hands on it come and build it here.

AI at Perk
AI is embedded in how we work across every function. The tools you'll use day-to-day are AI-enabled so you can move faster and spend more time on the work that matters. In practice, that means using AI to research and prioritise accounts, draft and refine outreach, handle customer interactions more effectively, synthesise information, and cut through shadow work - the invisible tasks that pull people away from the work only they can do - so you can focus on relationships and outcomes.

How We Work

At Perk, we take an IRL-first approach to work, where our team works together in-person 3 days a week. As such, this role requires you to be based within commuting distance of our hubs. We fundamentally believe in the value of meeting in real life to improve connectivity, productivity, creativity and ultimately making us a great place to work.

Great science regularly stalls in the clinic, not because the science is wrong, but because the company behind it lacks the capital, infrastructure, or focus to take it all the way through. Today’s clinical-stage biopharma model is broken, and as a result promising treatments never reach patients.

    • Contribute actively to the team’s processes and rituals, such as retrospectives and standups

    • Take on more complex coding and design tasks

    • Rotate through our support function, handling user issues and investigating and fixing bugs

    • Deepen your understanding of clinical trials, and build relationships across the wider company

🍊 What we offer

  • 30 days annual leave in addition to Bank Holidays, resulting in 39 paid days off per year

  • A well-stocked pantry and drinks fridge, Monday breakfast spread and catered team lunch on a Thursday for the UK office every week!

STARK is a defence technology company redefining the engineering and deployment of autonomous platforms. Your mission

At STARK, we are building the next generation of autonomous platforms capable of navigating the world's most contested environments. As a Senior Waveform Architect, you will own the entire development, architecture, and implementation of the waveform for our tactical anti-jam radio. In this critical role, you will ensure our communication links remain highly robust and operational under severe electronic countermeasure conditions.

  • Lead the design and implementation of the physical layer (PHY)—waveform, modulation, coding, framing, and synchronisation—from initial architecture to real-time execution.

Qualifications

  • You have practical experience debugging real radio links against physical hardware.


Nice to have

Our Opportunity

Over the past three years, Predium has built the leading real estate intelligence platform for ESG and value management in the DACH region - with the strongest names in the industry as customers: asset managers, housing companies, banks. Our customer base, our data, our credibility - that's valuable capital for the next step. Investment, credit, and asset management decisions in real estate are still made in Excel, case by case. We're now building the AI analyst that takes this work off people's hands - working directly on the customer's own data, scalable without adding headcount. We're well-funded, and we're bringing AI into real estate.


Your Mission

As a Senior Backend Engineer, you own the systems behind our platform: the GraphQL API, the relational data model, the background processing that turns customer documents and spreadsheets into structured data, and the permission model that lets a single owner and a bank with hundreds of portfolios use the same product. Most of your work runs from schema design all the way to the resolver.
You partner with product, design and other engineers to make sure we build what matters - not just what you have been told to do. You take real responsibility for production: when something is slow, you find out why, whether the answer is a bad query, application code or the infrastructure underneath.
You also help us make AI reliable in production. Document extraction, long-running analysis jobs and agentic features are core to where the product is going, and we need people who make these workflows testable and dependable rather than impressive in a demo.
Our company size of ~40 people ensures that the best idea wins and political discussions are kept aside. And every line of code helps to improve the carbon footprint of real estate properties.

Tech stack: TypeScript (NestJS backend, React frontend), Hasura/GraphQL, PostgreSQL (multiple databases incl. PostGIS), queue-based job processing, AWS (ECS / Elastic Beanstalk, S3, SES, Textract), IaC, Claude but all agents welcome


What you'll own

  • Build features across our Hasura GraphQL API, NestJS and Postgres. From schema design to resolver.
  • Model complex real estate and ESG domains in relational schemas. We run several Postgres databases side by side (one of them geospatial), and schema decisions here have consequences but also positive impact.
  • Own background processing: Excel imports, document extraction, long-running analysis jobs, 3D and image processing. Queues, retries, jobs that spawn other jobs - and figuring out what to do when step 3 of 7 fails at 2am.
  • Develop our permission model. Customers range from a single owner to enterprises with organization/portfolio/building-level access.
  • Integrate LLMs into backend workflows - especially document and data extraction - and make them reliable, verifyable and testable.
  • Debug production. Navigate Grafana dashboards and traces to find out why something is slow or failing, whether in the app, the CI/build pipeline or the infrastructure.
  • Spot overgrown or overly complex parts of the codebase and simplify them without being asked. Paying down complexity is part of the job.


What success looks like

  • You have shipped features end-to-end across schema, API and background processing that our customers actively use.
  • Our async processing (imports, extraction, analysis jobs) is measurably more robust: fewer silent failures, clear retry and recovery paths, and observability that tells us what broke and why.
  • You have taken ownership of at least one core area e.g. the permission model, the job orchestration layer or the LLM extraction pipeline and are the person the team goes to for it.
  • You have raised the bar on testing and developer experience in the backend, and other engineers ship faster because of you.
  • You are a trusted sparring partner for product and the team when we decide what to build and how.


What it takes

  • You're strong with Postgres. Schema design comes naturally, you can read a query plan, and you know when the ORM is lying to you. Geospatial experience is a bonus, not a requirement.
  • You're fluent in typed backend TypeScript. We work in NestJS and GraphQL every day; if your experience is in a comparable stack, that's fine, you'll pick it up fast.
  • You've built real queue-based processing. You designed workers, dealt with retries and partial failures, orchestrated multi-step workflows.
  • You've designed or worked with authorization for a multi-tenant product and know where it might get hairy.
  • You'd rather have one integration test that hits a real database schema than ten unit tests mocking everything. You write the test that catches the broken migration.
  • You treat production as a debuggable system. You can navigate dashboards and traces to figure out why something is slow, and you don't treat infrastructure as someone else's problem.
  • You communicate clearly - with engineers, product and, when needed, directly with customers.
  • You speak German at C1 level or better and English fluently. Our customers are German banks and asset managers, and you will talk to them.
Bonus:

  • AWS (S3, SES, ECS, RDS, …) and IaC.

  • LLMs in production, especially document or data extraction and making it reliable for actual user workflows.

Contexte de la Mission
Le pôle IS Data & Middleware est responsable des systèmes qui acheminent et façonnent les données. D'un côté se trouvent les plateformes de données qui alimentent l'analytique. De l'autre se trouve la couche middleware : connecteurs sur mesure, pipelines d'événements et services backend partagés qui distribuent les données aux systèmes de production gérés par d'autres départements, notamment IS Ventes, IS Opérations et IS Systèmes Clients.
Notre architecture repose sur un modèle évènementiel (event-driven). L'Event Data Hub transporte les événements métiers à travers l'entreprise. Autour de lui, nous concevons et exploitons les passerelles de données (data bridges) qui relient les systèmes sources et cibles, ainsi que les composants facilitateurs (enablers) permettant aux autres équipes de publier, consommer et utiliser la donnée de manière fiable.
La plateforme est déjà en production et fonctionne à grande échelle. Notre objectif actuel est d'étendre ses capacités, de connecter des systèmes supplémentaires et de garantir que les flux de données restent fiables, sécurisés et observables.

Objectif de la Mission
En tant que Développeur TypeScript, vous concevrez, construirez et exploiterez des passerelles de données et des composants de plateforme, en prenant en charge les fonctionnalités depuis le besoin métier initial jusqu'à la mise en production.
Vous collaborerez étroitement avec les business analysts, les product owners, les responsables systèmes et vos collègues ingénieurs. Réussir à ce poste nécessite de comprendre non seulement comment les flux de données sont mis en œuvre, mais aussi pourquoi ils existent et la valeur métier qu'ils apportent.
Il s'agit principalement d'un rôle d'ingénierie backend. Our Opportunity

Over the past three years, Predium has built the leading real estate intelligence platform for ESG and value management in the DACH region - with the strongest names in the industry as customers: asset managers, housing companies, banks. Our customer base, our data, our credibility - that's valuable capital for the next step. Investment, credit, and asset management decisions in real estate are still made in Excel, case by case. We're now building the AI analyst that takes this work off people's hands - working directly on the customer's own data, scalable without adding headcount. We're well-funded, and we're bringing AI into real estate.

Your Mission

As a Senior Backend Engineer, you own the systems behind our platform: the GraphQL API, the relational data model, the background processing that turns customer documents and spreadsheets into structured data, and the permission model that lets a single owner and a bank with hundreds of portfolios use the same product. Most of your work runs from schema design all the way to the resolver.
You partner with product, design and other engineers to make sure we build what matters - not just what you have been told to do. You take real responsibility for production: when something is slow, you find out why, whether the answer is a bad query, application code or the infrastructure underneath.
You also help us make AI reliable in production. Document extraction, long-running analysis jobs and agentic features are core to where the product is going, and we need people who make these workflows testable and dependable rather than impressive in a demo.
Our company size of ~40 people ensures that the best idea wins and political discussions are kept aside. And every line of code helps to improve the carbon footprint of real estate properties.

Tech stack: TypeScript (NestJS backend, React frontend), Hasura/GraphQL, PostgreSQL (multiple databases incl. PostGIS), queue-based job processing, AWS (ECS / Elastic Beanstalk, S3, SES, Textract), IaC, Claude but all agents welcome

What you'll own

  • Build features across our Hasura GraphQL API, NestJS and Postgres. From schema design to resolver.
  • Model complex real estate and ESG domains in relational schemas. We run several Postgres databases side by side (one of them geospatial), and schema decisions here have consequences but also positive impact.
  • Own background processing: Excel imports, document extraction, long-running analysis jobs, 3D and image processing. Queues, retries, jobs that spawn other jobs - and figuring out what to do when step 3 of 7 fails at 2am.
  • Develop our permission model. Customers range from a single owner to enterprises with organization/portfolio/building-level access.
  • Integrate LLMs into backend workflows - especially document and data extraction - and make them reliable, verifyable and testable.
  • Debug production. Navigate Grafana dashboards and traces to find out why something is slow or failing, whether in the app, the CI/build pipeline or the infrastructure.
  • Spot overgrown or overly complex parts of the codebase and simplify them without being asked. Paying down complexity is part of the job.

What success looks like

  • You have shipped features end-to-end across schema, API and background processing that our customers actively use.
  • Our async processing (imports, extraction, analysis jobs) is measurably more robust: fewer silent failures, clear retry and recovery paths, and observability that tells us what broke and why.
  • You have taken ownership of at least one core area e.g. the permission model, the job orchestration layer or the LLM extraction pipeline and are the person the team goes to for it.
  • You have raised the bar on testing and developer experience in the backend, and other engineers ship faster because of you.
  • You are a trusted sparring partner for product and the team when we decide what to build and how.

What it takes

  • You're strong with Postgres. Schema design comes naturally, you can read a query plan, and you know when the ORM is lying to you. Geospatial experience is a bonus, not a requirement.
  • You're fluent in typed backend TypeScript. We work in NestJS and GraphQL every day; if your experience is in a comparable stack, that's fine, you'll pick it up fast.
  • You've built real queue-based processing. You designed workers, dealt with retries and partial failures, orchestrated multi-step workflows.
  • You've designed or worked with authorization for a multi-tenant product and know where it might get hairy.
  • You'd rather have one integration test that hits a real database schema than ten unit tests mocking everything. You write the test that catches the broken migration.
  • You treat production as a debuggable system. You can navigate dashboards and traces to figure out why something is slow, and you don't treat infrastructure as someone else's problem.
  • You communicate clearly - with engineers, product and, when needed, directly with customers.
  • You speak German at C1 level or better and English fluently. Our customers are German banks and asset managers, and you will talk to them.

Bonus:

  • AWS (S3, SES, ECS, RDS, …) and IaC.

Traditional industrial manufacturing systems were built for predictability. Supply chains no longer are. Today, real-time data is buried in legacy tools that weren't designed for constant disruption. By the time an issue surfaces, it has already snowballed, sending everyone into firefighting mode. Pelico exists to close the gap between production plans and the daily reality on the factory floor.

We've built the manufacturing orchestration platform trusted by the world's most complex industrial operations : companies like Airbus, Boeing, Safran, Eaton, and Cartier. Our AI connects fragmented supply chain, production, and quality data into a single live operational picture — then puts AI agents to work anticipating disruptions, simulating recovery options, and keeping every team aligned before small problems become expensive ones.

Founded in 2019 and backed by General Catalyst, 83North, and Serena, we've raised $72M and are growing fast — 300% year-over-year revenue growth, deployed in 15+ countries, and supporting factories worldwide. We're headquartered in Paris, with offices in Miami, London and Amsterdam, and we're just getting started.

This is a rare chance to join a company that's redefining an industry that hasn't been disrupted in decades — from the inside.

About the Role

Pelico's customers feel one pain above all: missing parts that block delivery. The Solution squads are where we turn Pelico's platform into a product that fixes it. Each squad owns one solution surface — Material Coverage & inventory, Quality, Supplier & customer Collaboration / AI Buyer, MRO & Aftermarket, Program Management, or Strategic Account Support — composing our platform's building blocks into workflows that work across many customers. You'll lead one surface end to end: ship it fast, keep it configuration-first, and feed real customer patterns back into the platform — while our Regional Solution Engineering pods carry the day-to-day customer relationship.

You'll own a solution surface — and build it yourself:

  • Ship the surface. Compose configuration, compute, widgets, connectors, and agents into customer-facing workflows that pass a real acid test on real customers.

  • Harvest the field. Spot the patterns that recur across accounts and turn them into platform capabilities, so the next customer is faster.

  • Lead by example. Write the code, pair with your squad and the engineers deploying at customer sites, raise the bar, and grow the team as the impact you ship earns it.

Your impact: Customers buy outcomes — shortages caught, deliveries recovered, quality exceptions resolved. Your squad is where the platform becomes those outcomes. Own a surface well and you make Pelico's revenue engine both faster and more defensible — and you keep it from collapsing into bespoke work that can't scale.

About You

This is a lead-by-example role for a senior full-stack engineer with real product and customer judgment. You're energized by shipping outcomes under real constraints, you decide what not to build, and you lead by being in the code with your team.

You'll need:

  • A track record of shipping customer-facing product software end to end, full-stack, under real delivery pressure

  • Strong, current hands-on coding — we build in Kotlin / Java 25 (backend) and TypeScript / React (frontend); strong in one and credible across, or a fast learner

  • A configuration-first, anti-bespoke instinct — you build for many customers, not one fork at a time

Upvest empowers businesses to offer a wide range of investment products and the best experience in the field of capital market investment and retirement planning. Upvest’s Investment API is easy to integrate so that fintechs and financial institutions can save resources and fully focus on their core business.

We are proud to partner with Europe’s leading Fintechs and financial institutions such as DKB, Revolut, N26 and Raisin. Founded in 2017 by Martin Kassing, Upvest now brings together over 270 talented professionals from more than 70 nationalities. Upvest is backed by €280M in total funding from world-class investors, including BlackRock, Tencent, Sapphire Ventures, and Bessemer Venture Partners, Earlybird, Notion Capital, and Motive. Our latest €105M funding round in March 2026 - led by Sapphire and Tencent - serves as a massive catalyst for our growth, allowing us to offer premier investment experience.

About the role:

Team's mission

Upvest's core product is an API: the execution layer that moves securities for our clients. Upfront extends into the layer above it. It's Upvest's operational service panel for enterprise clients, giving their operations, support and compliance staff the ability to handle first-line requests themselves: looking into an end-user's account, checking what happened to an order, answering the question in front of them. Today their options are to ask Upvest support or to build a service panel of their own, which most of them won't do.

Our mission is to prove that financial institution customers can replace their fragmented operations with Upfront. That case isn't settled yet, and this team is the one making it. Our users do this work all day, so a clumsy interface is how a task turns back into a ticket for us. Our clients are already asking what AI can do for their operations teams. Agentic operations, exposed over MCP, is where we think this goes. What it should look like in Upfront is still open, and we'd like the person in this role to help define it.

Upfront is part of the Clients Tribe at Upvest. Together with the Public API and Tooling Apps teams we enable Upvest’s business to scale efficiently, accelerate our client’s time-to-market and embed intelligence and automation into client processes.

Your mission

You’ll focus on building what actually creates value for our clients. While our OKRs set the destination, we expect you to help map the route. We prioritize impact and shipping speed over a perfectly groomed backlog. Because you're on a client-facing team, the quality of your output directly impacts client trust – especially since we are handling their customers' money.

In our domain, the bar is high: anything touching client funds must be correct and auditable, or it's an incident. We will give you the client context, access, and autonomy to figure out what needs building, rather than just handing you a rigid spec. We also expect you to challenge our internal processes if they are slowing down your efficiency or shipping speed.

What you’ll do:

  • Take operational problems from concept to production, working across our React/TypeScript frontend and Go backend services.

  • Own modern interface security. Upfront is where external users act on real end-user data, so you will tackle per-client isolated environments, least-privilege access, and Auth0 integrations in a regulated space.

  • Expand the operational surface across Upvest's internal domains and develop a deep understanding of how our core systems piece together.

  • Help define how software delivery works in an AI-enabled company by pushing AI tooling to its limits to maximize quality and speed while staying compliant.

  • Build agentic operations as we move toward exposing Upfront over MCP. Every action requires a strict audit trail, so you will solve real design problems around what an agent can do autonomously versus what requires human intervention.

  • Work in weekly cycles with bi-weekly retrospectives to prioritize high-quality, high-frequency shipping.

     

What you bring:

  • A strong product engineering mindset where you care about the "why" just as much as the "how" and proactively bring ideas to the table.

  • Solid backend experience in Go, Java, or Kotlin (we build in Go but will give you time to ramp up).

  • Practical experience building modern client-facing interfaces using React and TypeScript.

  • Experience building products that require per-customer configuration without devolving into a custom fork per client.

  • Deep knowledge of authentication, authorization, and security best practices.

  • A strong focus on quality, extensibility, and automated testing.

  • True end-to-end ownership across containers, CI/CD pipelines, and relational data modeling.

  • A working understanding of event-driven architectures.

  • A pragmatic approach to engineering and the ability to make smart tradeoffs under constraints.

  • Real-world experience using AI tools to drive software engineering workflows, not only writing code snippets .

  • The ability to navigate undefined problems and align other teams without needing formal authority.

     

It’s great if you have:

  • Experience with Investment products or the Fintech domain, in general.

  • Experience building operational or back-office tooling for business users.

  • Experience with identity platforms such as Auth0, or with multi-tenant isolation.

  • Experience with operating services in a decoupled, event-driven system, leveraging modern observability tooling (e.g. monitoring and tracing).

     

How we Upvest in you:

  • Best-in-class AI tools: Every Upvenger has €20,000 per year to spend on the best AI tools available — so you're always working with the most powerful models and tooling on the market.

  • Impact-driven work: We’re building the infrastructure that will power the future of investing in Europe. It’s complex, ambitious, and meaningful. You’ll work with modern technologies and create something entirely new. No legacy systems, no limits.

  • Wellbeing: Recharge with 30 days of annual leave and maintain a healthy lifestyle with sports benefits. Access confidential professional coaching and enjoy the flexibility to work remotely abroad for up to 183 days a year. Recharge with UpRest, a one-month fully paid sabbatical after every 4 years of working at Upvest.

  • Development: Growth is in our DNA. Each Upvenger has access to a personal development budget and the freedom to decide how to use it.

  • Flexible work environment: Work from any of our hubs in Berlin, London or Tallinn hybrid or remotely across Europe, depending on the role. We give you the choice and budget to work where you’re most comfortable and productive, either at home or in the office. You choose.

  • Compensation and equity: We believe that all Upvengers contribute to our success and deserve a competitive, above-market salary and a participation in our employee equity program.

  • Team celebrations: Participate in company-wide events, such as UpFest, dinners, offsites and our Holiday party, to connect with colleagues and celebrate our achievements.

  • Inclusion: We’re committed to a culture where everyone belongs and thrives. Our Employee Resources Groups foster inclusion and connection, like Upfem for our female Upvengers, or UpVergent supporting neurodivergent Upvengers and allies.

Our Values:

  • Make it easy for others. We simplify the complex and act with the best intentions.

  • Own the outcome. We are proactive, fast and confident to get the job done, valuing progress over perfection.

  • Rise to the challenge. We aim high and push the boundaries. We stay curious, learn and celebrate our wins together.

  • Tell the story. We start with the Why to align on purpose. We are transparent and share knowledge to empower and inspire others.
